messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — High memory pressure detected on runtime-infer-01.gpu0. Error rate rising for /v1/generate. Auto-escalation: page oncall.

maria: oncall here. Seeing OOMs and page faults on gpu0, multiple pods restarted in the last 3m. marking impact: degraded tail latency for a subset of customer traffic. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre.

ash: grabbing logs now. which stack? kv-cache + runtime or allocator churn?

maria: initial indicators point at GPU fragmentation + KV cache growth. eviction counts are flat while incoming QPS had a short spike. customers affected: 2 mid-market clusters with long chats -> heavy KV prefix reuse.

sam: sharing an excerpt of recent metrics: 
```
GPU0 free_mem_mb: [120, 118, 60, 24, 8, OOM]
kv_cache_entries: 3.2M -> 3.2M
kv_evictions_total: 0.0
batch_size_95p: 12
alloc_retry_count: 23
page_faults/sec: 180
```

jordan: interesting that kv_evictions_total stayed 0. do we have a bug where eviction threshold wasn't applied because of a policy mismatch? seen this before if config has kv_eviction_mode=off during deploy.

ash: checking current runtime args on the node:
```
ps aux | grep runtime
--model runtime-v2 --kv-cache-enabled --kv-eviction=auto --kv-eviction-threshold=0.9 --batch-limit=16
```

maria: threshold 0.9 seems high when batch spikes to 12-16. hypothesis A: big batches + high threshold cause large transient allocations that fragment GPU heap and prevent timely eviction -> OOM. Hypothesis B: KV eviction path might be stuck due to lock contention in the eviction thread.

srebot: Added incident timeline entry: 1709234567 - pager raised; 1709234602 - first pod restart; 1709234660 - ops mitigation 1 executed; 1709234740 - partial stabilization.

ash: running live check on eviction loop (remote exec):
```
kubectl exec -it runtime-infer-01 -- curl http://localhost:9000/debug/kv/metrics
# returns last_gc_ts: 0, eviction_paused: false, eviction_lock_waits: 120
```

sam: uploaded full logs to s3: https://s3.company.internal/incidents/1709234567/logs.tar.gz (contains allocator, runtime, batch profiler)

maria: mitigation steps I'm rolling now:
- lower batch-limit to 2 on runtime-infer-01
- toggle kv-eviction-threshold to 0.6
- enable aggressive kv eviction preset: kv_evict_fast
- start a single warm standby node to move traffic

ash: command I used to update config (in case we need to revert):
```
kubectl patch deploy runtime --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/1/value","value":"2"}]'
```

jordan: after batch-limit=2 and kv_evict_fast, observed immediate drop in allocation retries and fragmentation numbers. GPU free memory stabilized around 80-100MB. tail latency still elevated for warm requests but no new OOMs in 10m.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied by maria at 1709234688. Autoscaler: scaled up runtime-infer-02 to absorb traffic.

maria: customer impact note: two customers reported intermittent 503s between 1709234560-1709234680. I opened tickets and attached logs.

sam: quick analysis from logs: during spike we had a single request with embedded long context that caused batch aggregation to pack 4 requests of 3k tokens each -> huge KV growth. Suggest we add a hard per-request token cap at the proxy to avoid pathological packing.

ash: created PR to add per-request token cap and fallback to streamed-mode if above 2k tokens: https://git.company/repo/pull/5421 (wip)

maria: for now action items before handoff:
- follow up RCA to reproduce fragmentation in staging with synthetic batched long contexts
- confirm eviction thread health across nodes
- add per-request token cap in proxy canary
- document customer mitigation timeline and communication

leo: taking night oncall at 1709234800. what's the current status and things to watch?

maria: handing off to @leo — system stabilized after batch lowering and kv_evict_fast. Watch for: any new OOMs, kv_evictions_total remaining low, sudden batch spikes. If OOM returns, rollback kv_evict_fast and scale to extra nodes then page SRE.

leo: ack. will monitor dashboards and watch the S3 log bundle. please add a short note in the incident board with suspected root cause: batch aggregation + high eviction threshold -> fragmentation + delayed eviction.

jordan: recording timeline and hypothesis in the post-incident doc. I'll collect heap dumps and allocator traces from s3 bundle for offline RCA.

maria: thanks all. closing live triage, handing off to RCA owners. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated -> under RCA. Follow-up owner: jordan. Severity: Sev2.
